Pattern: Ines's mug location.
Assumption: I repeatedly defaulted to cupboard_k1, assuming it was stored there or following a kitchen-centric path.
Reality: On day 11, the mug was at kitchen_table_k1 (07:52), coffee_table_l1 (14:26), and coffee_table_l1 (21:29). It is frequently in the living room, not the kitchen cupboard.
Correction: Stop defaulting to cupboard_k1. The mug is highly volatile but currently favors coffee_table_l1 and kitchen_table_k1. Check coffee_table_l1 first for afternoon/evening queries. If unsure, ABSTAIN.

Pattern: Ines's glass location.
Assumption: I defaulted to coffee_table_l1 for evening queries, assuming it stayed in the living room.
Reality: On day 11, the glass was at kitchen_table_k1 at 19:35. This contradicts the day 10 trend of it being at nightstand_b1 late at night, showing high variability.
Correction: The glass moves between kitchen_table_k1, coffee_table_l1, and nightstand_b1. Do not default to the living room for evening. Check kitchen_table_k1 and nightstand_b1 as primary candidates. If unsure, ABSTAIN.

Pattern: Ines's book location.
Assumption: I guessed bedroom_floor_b1, assuming she was reading in bed.
Reality: On day 10, the book was at armchair_l1. No new data on day 11, but the living room preference remains the strongest signal.
Correction: Books are often in the living room (armchair_l1, couch_l1) rather than the bedroom floor. Check living room seating first. If unsure, ABSTAIN.

Pattern: Generalization error regarding Ines's items.
Assumption: I treated items as having stable locations or predictable daily paths.
Reality: Items move independently and frequently. The mug and glass were in different rooms at similar times on day 11.
Correction: Track each item individually. Do not assume that because one item is in the kitchen, other items are in the same room. Always consider the specific item's recent history. If the item has moved multiple times in the last few hours, ABSTAIN rather than guessing.
